chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Abdullah, who said: Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marwazi narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan (the First Imam), peace be upon him, who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever memorizes forty traditions from my ummah that they need for the affairs of their religion, Allah, Exalted and Mighty, will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment as a jurist and a scholar.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for memorizing forty hadiths in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the Shia emphasis on the transmission of prophetic traditions as a means of achieving scholarly authority, linking the preservation of knowledge directly to divine recognition on the Day of Judgment. It reflects the tradition of 'ilm (knowledge) as a sacred trust, where memorizing forty key narrations serves as a foundational qualification for becoming a faqih, thereby ensuring the continuity of religious guidance within the community.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s.) narrates that the Messenger of Allah  (s.a.w.s.)  said,  “Allah  will  resurrect  on  the  Day  of Judgment as a jurist and a scholar one who memorizes forty traditions as a part of a commandment of his religion.”
